messages:
maya: Heads-up — several eval PRs failing intermittently in GH Actions matrix. root failure is 'runner: resource not found' on 2/5 matrix runs.

gha-bot: [CI] run failed — see https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/123456789 (reaction :eyes:)

arul: I saw this too. Seems correlated with matrix parallelism + ephemeral cache restore.

maya: repro steps: push branch -> gha matrix 5x (quantize+eval) -> 2 jobs time out waiting for /dev/shm mount.

sandeep: Could be the runner image pulling a heavy wheel and hitting disk quota. Any logs? Can you paste the job logs?

maya: paste logs:
```
Error: failed to prepare image: write /tmp/overlay/...: no space left on device
Runner: ubuntu-22.04-hosted
Steps: setup-python, restore-cache, pip install -r requirements.txt
```

eva: If heavy installs are the issue, option A) switch to prebuilt container image in GH Actions, B) run heavyweight evals in nightly Buildkite, keep PR gate as a fast smoke.

arul: Agreed. Proposal:
- Keep PR gating: a lightweight eval matrix (unit evals + smoke generation, ~2m)
- Nightly: full eval matrix with quantize variants on Buildkite
- Use self-hosted runners for nightly heavy jobs

maya: Draft GH workflow snippet for smoke gate:
```
name: PR-eval-smoke
on: pull_request
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        eval: [smoke, unit]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Use container
        run: docker pull ghcr.io/redwood/eval-smoke:2026-03-18
      - run: ./run_eval --smoke
```

sandeep: Can we add a cache key per matrix axis to avoid collisions? like `cache-{{ matrix.eval }}-{{ runner.os }}`

maya: Good call. I'll open PR to replace the current GH Actions matrix with this gating config and add a Buildkite job for nightly full matrix. Assigning to @arul to wire Buildkite.

buildkite-bot: Buildkite pipeline created: infra/evals-nightly. First run scheduled 2026-03-19 03:00 UTC.

eva: Also add an alert on eval regression metric flakiness (stderr variance > threshold) so we don't treat infra flakes as model regressions.

maya: noted. thanks all :tada:
